institutionName: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The outdoor adventures, skiing, hiking, and experiencing "friluftsliv" as the norwegians do it. But also because their landscape is extra, and it is very relevant for my studies to look at landscapes.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Everything was so nice, the lectures, the people, the outdoors - so cool

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: All the paperwork was hard, but there was plenty of information and we just had to find the right people for our qustions

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had 2-3 days of welcoming from the university, with a LOT of information about everything, from housing to lectures and field trips. But the people from the welcoming days were around the university, so that we could contact them if we had questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was nice and fun, but very long days, with at lot of informations.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Samskipnaden in Norway - so easy! This is the cheapest and easiest way for exchange students, so I would definitely recommend

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Samskipnaden has all the information you need, but be aware that samskipnaden is not 1 housing, it is a lot of different gousing, so if you have prefrences for which part of the city and so, you should look into that.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very clean, nice, and close to university - but very hard to get the key from some misunderstandings.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registration before leaving home was easy, but selecting courses and preparing at the university was not as easy.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: No one had a clue about who we were supposed to talk to, and they didn't prepare the courses and registartion for courses which made it quite difficult.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not really anything, it was hard to find an office with people that would help with courses and admittion - only the students from the welcoming, and they really tried to help but they didn't know about registration for the courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I ended up happy about the corses, but it was hard communicating with the university about it.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It takes time, but everyone involved wants it to end well for all, so there won't be unsolveable problems, it just takes time

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was nice, there was a lot of relevant stuff for my studies

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Easy - there was new subjects but not to difficult, which gave me time to experience the culture and the people around me

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot different, but nice to experience

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Snow and avalanche science
GIS i arealplanlegging
Geografi og samfund

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The avalanche science course - because it is very norwegian but still tort in english with an american professor. And you get to go on a field trip in the norwegian wilderness

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They really offered a lot, and i went on some weekend trips, very nice

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything, I didn't find anything that i missed

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Just do what you think is fun - but skiing because I think it is fun, and because it is very norwegian

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go skiing!!! or hiking, or anything outdoors

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy - but I am from Denmark, so maybe our cultures are also quite close to eachother

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Come to the events, there is a lot of international students

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Language, that is the only thing I can think of

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Skiing, and in general their "friluftsliv"

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Have fun, don't get hung up by school, go skiing

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sure, but i dont know what

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The other danes, that I cold take home with me

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The fieldtrips, but they were also the coolest part

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Try to keep up with all the offers, there might be something just for you - example could be waffle day every other week

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
